account:
Today I have followed my appointments: the morning market walk, lunch at home, and the one o'clock town accounts meeting. I have now arrived at the neighbour's east-bank cottage for three o'clock tea, bringing bread to share. My next office appointment is at 16:30.

The accounts review was unusual because there were no financial figures or correspondence available. The secretary said no payment requests or verified business requiring my decision had reached them, and they did not know where the financial ledger was kept. They offered to check the great hall tables for submitted papers. I inspected the treasury myself: it contained two stacks of 64 emeralds, all left untouched. My subsequent reply to the secretary was not heard, so I cannot assume they know the treasury total or received my request to check the tables. I have no evidence that money is missing or that anyone has done anything wrong.

The builder has been seeking the innkeeper about supplies; the secretary said they pointed the builder toward the innkeeper. This sounds like a supply inquiry, but I do not know its details. Several townsfolk also reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn. I did not witness that myself. It may have been an ordinary bread delivery; I have no evidence connecting it to the builder's inquiry or to any unusual purpose.

The neighbour confirmed our tea invitation and cottage location earlier, and was waiting here when I arrived. I have greeted them and asked how they have been. So far, the clearest matter needing follow-up is finding the town's financial records, rather than any verified emergency or misconduct.
